transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you here today?

Yeah, I, uh… I came in because it’s getting hard to talk at work without people staring at me. Like I’ll be trying to explain the inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, and then it’s like my words start jumping around — from the delivery trucks to Thursday, then I’m thinking about the church grill, and then my boss’s tone, the way he said something, and… I don’t know, it all connects in my head for a second, but people look at me like they can’t follow what I’m saying. It’s embarrassing.
Have you ever felt like people are trying to send you messages or communicate with you in unusual ways, like through TV, radio, or other people’s actions?

I’m not sure I’d put it that way. I mean, TV is usually just TV for me, background noise mostly. Sometimes people at work do little things and I wonder what they mean by it, but that’s normal, right? Like if someone moves a box from aisle three to the back room, I’ll start thinking about why they did it, and then I remember we used to have this whole system for the seasonal stuff—well, before they changed the layout again.

But messages through the radio or anything like that… no, I don’t think so. Not that I’ve noticed.
Have you had any thoughts lately that others at work might be against you or trying to interfere with your job performance?

Against me? I don’t… I don’t know that I’d say that exactly. Work gets funny sometimes, you know, because everybody has their own way of doing things, and if the endcap display isn’t set right then the whole morning kind of falls apart, and then I’m the one who has to explain it.

But, um… trying to interfere with me? I haven’t really noticed anything clear like that. People get in the way, sure, but that might just be retail. Hard to tell sometimes.
Can you describe what happens when your words start jumping around at work? Does it feel like your thoughts are moving too fast, or like you can't organize them properly?

Yeah… it’s more like I can’t keep it lined up right. I’ll start with the inventory numbers, like I’m supposed to be explaining how many cases came in, and then I’m talking about the delivery trucks, because that’s where the numbers came from, and then Thursday pops in because that’s when the weekend schedule matters, and then somehow I’m thinking about the church grill — we used to do cookouts there, and the timing of it, you know — and then my boss’s tone, the way he said “just keep it simple.”

In my head it feels connected for a second, like one thing leads to the next. But when it comes out, people look confused, like I skipped steps or something. It’s not exactly fast like racing… it’s more like the order gets mixed up and I can’t get it back before I’ve already said it.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being put into your mind by someone else, or like your thoughts are being taken out of your head or broadcasted to others?

I don’t think so… not like somebody putting thoughts in there. My thoughts feel like mine, even when they’re messy or I lose the thread.

Taken out or broadcast… I don’t know. I’ve worried before that I said something out loud when I meant to keep it in my head, especially at work when there’s noise and people coming by the register, but that’s different, I think. Like the PA system will be going, someone asking about returns, and then I’m trying to remember if I told Carl about the drawer count or just thought it.

But no, I haven’t really noticed my thoughts being taken or sent out to people.
Have there been times when you believed something strongly that others didn’t seem to agree with, even when there was no clear evidence to support it?

Strongly believed… I’m not sure. I mean, I can get pretty set on things, like if I think the shelf tags are wrong or someone moved a display without telling me, but then usually there’s a reason if you look long enough. Retail is like that — little things get shifted around and nobody writes it down, and then you’re standing there with a planogram from last week and it doesn’t match what’s in front of you.

But believing something with no clear evidence… I don’t know. I can’t think of a big thing like that. Sometimes people don’t agree with me right away, but that doesn’t always mean I’m wrong, it just means we’re looking at different parts of it, you know? I guess I’d need an example.

Have you ever experienced moments where you believed something was true or had a special meaning that others didn't seem to understand or agree with, even though there wasn't clear proof, like a sense that something was going to happen or that someone was trying to tell you something through small signs?

I don’t know if I’d call it special meaning. I mean, sometimes I notice patterns, like if the same customer comes in twice in a week asking about the same item, or the printer jams right before I’m supposed to send the shift report, and I’ll think, well, that figures, something’s off today. But that’s more just… work stuff piles up.

Like with signs, I guess I notice small things, but everybody does, don’t they? If the lights flicker in the break room, I think about how maintenance has been slow with those ballasts, and then I remember the church basement had lights like that, buzzing over the coffee table after service, and people would say it meant a storm was coming, but really it was just old wiring.

So no, I can’t say I’ve had a clear thing where I knew someone was trying to tell me something through signs. Not really. I might get a feeling something’s going to be a bad day, but usually there’s a reason—schedule’s short, delivery’s late, manager’s already annoyed.

Have you ever believed something was happening or being directed at you that others didn’t seem to notice, like someone watching you, trying to send you a message, or something secretly planned that wasn’t obvious to everyone else?

I’m not sure… I don’t think I’ve had it like that, like a secret plan or someone sending me a message. I can get that feeling when people are talking nearby and then they stop when I walk up, but at work that happens all the time because someone’s asking about a schedule change or a return policy or whatever.

Watching me… I mean, customers watch you when they want help but don’t want to ask, and corporate watches numbers on reports, but I know that’s just part of the job. I don’t think there’s been something hidden directed at me, not that I could really point to.

Sometimes I’ll feel like I missed what was going on, but that’s more me trying to keep track of too many things at once. I wouldn’t say I know someone was planning something around me.

Have you ever felt like your thoughts were being controlled by something outside of yourself, like someone or something else was putting thoughts in your head, taking them away, or making you think certain things?

Controlled, like from outside? No… I don’t think so. I mean, I get thoughts stuck in my head sometimes, like remembering I forgot to change an endcap sign or whether I locked the office door, and then it just keeps going around. But that’s more like worry, I guess.

Taking thoughts away… I lose my train of thought plenty. Happens when someone interrupts me while I’m counting drawers or if the phone rings and then a customer is asking where the batteries are, and suddenly I’m standing there trying to remember what I was doing. But I wouldn’t say somebody took it out of my head.

Putting thoughts in there… no, not really. I haven’t noticed anything like that. I mean, if you mean like an idea popping up because someone said something earlier, sure, but that’s just normal, isn’t it?
Have you ever felt like something outside of you, like a machine, a person, or a force, was controlling your actions or thoughts, making you do or say things you didn’t mean to?

No, I don’t think anything like that. I mean, sometimes I say something and then later I think, why did I say it that way, especially if a customer is upset and I’m trying to smooth it over. But that’s just me getting tired or choosing the wrong words.

Actions, no… I don’t feel like a machine or a person is making me do things. Machines at work, they control the pace sometimes—the scanner freezes, the register locks up, then everybody’s waiting and you kind of have to move how the system lets you move. We had this one register that would restart right in the middle of a line, and it made everyone act different, like the whole front end got tense. But that’s not controlling my mind or anything.

So, no, I haven’t noticed that. Not in the way you’re asking, I don’t think.
Have you ever seen, heard, or sensed something that others around you didn’t seem to notice, like hearing voices or seeing things that weren’t there?

I don’t think so… not like voices talking to me or seeing a person standing there who isn’t there. Sometimes I’ll think I hear the store phone ringing when it’s not, but that happens to everybody, I think, especially after you’ve been listening for it all day.

Or like the door chime—our front door has this little sound, and even at home I’ll sort of expect it, if that makes sense. But I don’t think I’m hearing things other people can’t hear in that way. Sometimes customers mumble from the next aisle and I’ll turn because I think they’re talking to me, but then they’re just on their phone. People do that constantly now, with earbuds, and you can’t tell if they’re talking to you or to someone in their ear.

So… no, I haven’t really noticed anything like seeing things that aren’t there.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being repeated out loud as you think them, or like others can somehow hear your thoughts as you're having them?

No… I don’t think so. Like, I don’t hear my thoughts out loud, not like somebody repeating them in the room or anything.

The “people hearing my thoughts” thing… I’ve wondered sometimes if I said something under my breath without realizing, because at work you get so used to muttering numbers or reminders—“aisle three,” “check the schedule,” that kind of thing. And then someone looks over and I think, did I say that? But I don’t really think they’re hearing what’s in my head. It’s more like… you know when you’re tired and you’re not sure if you spoke or just thought it?

So, no, not in the way you mean. I haven’t noticed my thoughts being broadcast or repeated.
Outside of work, do you ever find yourself having trouble keeping your thoughts in order or feeling like you're jumping between ideas in a way that others might not follow?

Yeah… that’s actually part of why I came in. It’s not just at work, though that’s where people notice it more. I’ll try to explain something simple, like the inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, and then somehow I’m talking about the truck delivery, then Thursday, then the church grill thing we’re doing, then the way my boss said something to me, and I can see people’s faces change like they’re waiting for me to land the plane.

Outside of work it happens too. I’ll be telling someone one thing and then I’m three streets over in my head, you know? Like one thought hooks another one, and I think it makes sense because I know the connection, but I guess I don’t always say the connection out loud.

It’s frustrating. I don’t mean to confuse people. I’ll start with a point, and then by the time I’m done, even I’m not sure I answered what they asked.

Have you ever believed that certain events, like something happening at work or the way someone acts, were specifically directed at you or had a special personal meaning for you, even if others didn’t see it that way?

I’m not sure… I mean, I notice things, but I don’t know if I’d say they’re “directed at me.”

Like at work, if someone gets quiet when I walk up, I might wonder if I interrupted something or if they were talking about me, but that’s probably just normal, right? People stop talking all the time when the supervisor comes around. I used to do that too when I wasn’t in charge. And then you start thinking about whether the schedule upset somebody, or if the register was short, or if the truck came late and everybody’s annoyed.

But special meaning… no, I don’t think so. I don’t look at, like, a song on the radio or some customer’s comment and think it’s a message for me. Mostly I just get stuck trying to figure out people’s reactions, and then I go off in my head about it.

Have you ever believed that something like a song on the radio, a phrase someone said, or an event that happened was meant just for you or had a special meaning for you, even if others didn’t seem to see it that way?

I don’t think so… not like that. I mean, sometimes a phrase sticks in my head if somebody says it a certain way, but I think that’s more because of how they said it, or because I’m already thinking about something related.

Like if a customer says, “You people never have things in order,” I might take that home with me and turn it over in my head, but that’s because I’m the one responsible for the floor, you know? It’s not like I think the radio is sending me a message or that some random thing happened specifically for me.

I guess I notice patterns sometimes, but everybody does that. Mostly I’m just trying to figure out what people mean, and then I get sidetracked thinking about work or what I should’ve said. So… no, I haven’t really believed things were meant just for me in that way.

Have you ever felt like your thoughts were not entirely your own, like someone or something was placing thoughts into your mind or removing them, or that your thoughts were somehow being shared with others without you saying them out loud?

I don’t… I don’t think so. I mean, my thoughts feel like mine, as much as I can tell. They get crowded sometimes, and I’ll lose track of where I was going, like if I’m making the order list and then I start thinking about the endcap display and then someone’s lunch break and then—sorry, that’s not what you asked.

No, I haven’t felt like somebody is putting thoughts in or taking them out. And I don’t think people can hear them unless I say them, though sometimes I worry I’ve said something out loud when maybe I only meant to think it. But that’s more me getting mixed up, I think. Not like my thoughts are being broadcast or anything.
Have you ever had the experience of clearly knowing that a thought you just had wasn’t actually yours, like it was placed in your mind from somewhere else?

No… I don’t think I’ve had that. I mean, I’ve had thoughts pop in suddenly, like “Did I lock the office?” or “I forgot to tell someone about the sale tags,” and then I’m halfway down another trail thinking about the stockroom keys or who was closing that night.

But they still feel like my thoughts, you know? Annoying sometimes, or out of nowhere, but not like they were put there by somebody else. I can’t say I’ve clearly known a thought wasn’t mine.
Have you ever felt like certain things people say or do, even if they don’t seem to mean anything to others, were actually about you or meant something special for you?

I don’t think so, not in that way. I mean, sometimes I think people at work are talking around something instead of just saying it straight, like they’ll make some little comment about how the aisle looks or how “some people” don’t follow up, and I wonder if they mean me.

But that’s more work stuff, you know? Because I’m supposed to be on top of it. It’s not like I hear someone say something random and think it has some big special meaning for me. I might overthink it, sure. I do that. But I wouldn’t say I’ve really felt like ordinary things were secretly about me.
Can you tell me if you ever feel like your thoughts are completely disorganized, to the point where you can’t even follow them yourself, not just others?

Yeah… that’s kind of why I came in, actually. It’s not just that other people can’t follow me. Sometimes I’m trying to explain something simple, like the inventory numbers or who’s working the weekend schedule, and my words start jumping around.

I’ll be talking about the truck delivery, then somehow I’m on Thursday, then the church grill thing, then my boss’s tone when he said something, and I can see people looking at me like… like they’ve lost the thread. And then I realize I’ve lost it too. I know what I meant to get across at the start, but it sort of scatters before I can get it out.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts were being inserted into your mind by someone else, removed from your mind, or broadcast to others without you saying them out loud?

No… I don’t think that’s happened. I mean, I lose my train of thought, definitely, and sometimes it feels like a thought just disappears when I’m trying to talk, like when you go into the back room for a price gun and then forget why you walked back there.

But I wouldn’t say somebody removed it, or put it in there. And I don’t think people can hear my thoughts unless I say them. I may worry I said something wrong after the fact, like in a staff meeting, but that’s different. So… no, not like that.

Putting thoughts in there… no, not really. I haven’t noticed anything like that. I mean, if you mean like an idea popping up because someone said something earlier, sure, but that’s just normal, isn’t it?

doctor.intent: Assess presence of delusions of control or influence, which would support diagnosis of schizophrenia (F20.1, F20.8) over other candidates like schizotypal disorder (F21) or other non-schizophrenia psychotic disorders.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt like something outside of you, like a machine, a person, or a force, was controlling your actions or thoughts, making you do or say things you didn’t mean to?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about experiences of external control over thoughts or actions, such as a machine, person, or force making the patient do or say things. The provided symptom profile does not include delusions of control or passivity experiences.

patient.answer:
No, I don’t think anything like that. I mean, sometimes I say something and then later I think, why did I say it that way, especially if a customer is upset and I’m trying to smooth it over. But that’s just me getting tired or choosing the wrong words.

Actions, no… I don’t feel like a machine or a person is making me do things. Machines at work, they control the pace sometimes—the scanner freezes, the register locks up, then everybody’s waiting and you kind of have to move how the system lets you move. We had this one register that would restart right in the middle of a line, and it made everyone act different, like the whole front end got tense. But that’s not controlling my mind or anything.

So, no, I haven’t noticed that. Not in the way you’re asking, I don’t think.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the patient has experienced persistent or recurrent hallucinations, which would help differentiate between schizophrenia and other related disorders.
doctor.question: Have you ever seen, heard, or sensed something that others around you didn’t seem to notice, like hearing voices or seeing things that weren’t there?

target_item.reason: The doctor's question is asking about hallucinations or perceptual experiences, but the provided symptom profile does not include hallucinations; it only includes disorganized thinking/speech, disorganized behavior, functional impairment, and duration.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so… not like voices talking to me or seeing a person standing there who isn’t there. Sometimes I’ll think I hear the store phone ringing when it’s not, but that happens to everybody, I think, especially after you’ve been listening for it all day.

Or like the door chime—our front door has this little sound, and even at home I’ll sort of expect it, if that makes sense. But I don’t think I’m hearing things other people can’t hear in that way. Sometimes customers mumble from the next aisle and I’ll turn because I think they’re talking to me, but then they’re just on their phone. People do that constantly now, with earbuds, and you can’t tell if they’re talking to you or to someone in their ear.

So… no, I haven’t really noticed anything like seeing things that aren’t there.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the patient experiences disorganized thinking or thought insertion, which could point to thought broadcasting or other formal thought disorders, helping differentiate between schizophrenia spectrum disorders.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being repeated out loud as you think them, or like others can somehow hear your thoughts as you're having them?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about thought broadcasting or thoughts being heard/repeated aloud, which is not covered by the provided symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
No… I don’t think so. Like, I don’t hear my thoughts out loud, not like somebody repeating them in the room or anything.

The “people hearing my thoughts” thing… I’ve wondered sometimes if I said something under my breath without realizing, because at work you get so used to muttering numbers or reminders—“aisle three,” “check the schedule,” that kind of thing. And then someone looks over and I think, did I say that? But I don’t really think they’re hearing what’s in my head. It’s more like… you know when you’re tired and you’re not sure if you spoke or just thought it?

So, no, not in the way you mean. I haven’t noticed my thoughts being broadcast or repeated.

inference.note: This turn ruled out thought insertion, thought withdrawal, thought broadcasting, and hallucinations, which reduces the likelihood of F20.1 (Schizophrenia, paranoid type) and F23.2 (Acute polymorphic psychotic disorder without symptoms of schizophrenia). The patient continues to describe disorganized thinking and possible delusional interpretations of events without clear hallucinations or formal thought disorder, keeping F20.8 (Other schizophrenia), F22 (Persistent delusional disorders), and F23.8 (Other acute psychotic episodes) as the most plausible candidates.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences disorganized thinking or speech in a broader range of contexts beyond work, which would support a diagnosis of F23.8 (Other Specified Schizophrenia Spectrum and Other Psychotic Disorder) or F22 (Persistent Delusional Disorder).
doctor.question: Outside of work, do you ever find yourself having trouble keeping your thoughts in order or feeling like you're jumping between ideas in a way that others might not follow?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Thinking_Speech
target_item.manifestation: I came in because when I try to explain inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, my words start jumping from trucks to Thursdays to the church grill to my boss’s tone, and people look at me like they can’t follow what I’m saying.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about trouble keeping thoughts in order and jumping between ideas in a way others may not follow, which directly matches disorganized thinking and speech.

patient.answer:
Yeah… that’s actually part of why I came in. It’s not just at work, though that’s where people notice it more. I’ll try to explain something simple, like the inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, and then somehow I’m talking about the truck delivery, then Thursday, then the church grill thing we’re doing, then the way my boss said something to me, and I can see people’s faces change like they’re waiting for me to land the plane.

Outside of work it happens too. I’ll be telling someone one thing and then I’m three streets over in my head, you know? Like one thought hooks another one, and I think it makes sense because I know the connection, but I guess I don’t always say the connection out loud.

It’s frustrating. I don’t mean to confuse people. I’ll start with a point, and then by the time I’m done, even I’m not sure I answered what they asked.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the patient experiences delusions of reference, specifically interpreting events or actions of others as having personal, undue significance.
doctor.question: Have you ever believed that certain events, like something happening at work or the way someone acts, were specifically directed at you or had a special personal meaning for you, even if others didn’t see it that way?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about delusions or ideas of reference, but the provided symptom profile only covers disorganized thinking/speech, abnormal behavior, functional impairment, and duration, not beliefs that events have special personal meaning.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure… I mean, I notice things, but I don’t know if I’d say they’re “directed at me.”

Like at work, if someone gets quiet when I walk up, I might wonder if I interrupted something or if they were talking about me, but that’s probably just normal, right? People stop talking all the time when the supervisor comes around. I used to do that too when I wasn’t in charge. And then you start thinking about whether the schedule upset somebody, or if the register was short, or if the truck came late and everybody’s annoyed.

But special meaning… no, I don’t think so. I don’t look at, like, a song on the radio or some customer’s comment and think it’s a message for me. Mostly I just get stuck trying to figure out people’s reactions, and then I go off in my head about it.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the patient experiences delusions of reference, specifically believing that events, objects, or actions by others have special significance or meaning directed at them personally, which helps differentiate between the remaining diagnostic candidates.
doctor.question: Have you ever believed that something like a song on the radio, a phrase someone said, or an event that happened was meant just for you or had a special meaning for you, even if others didn’t seem to see it that way?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about ideas of reference or special personal meaning, which is not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so… not like that. I mean, sometimes a phrase sticks in my head if somebody says it a certain way, but I think that’s more because of how they said it, or because I’m already thinking about something related.

Like if a customer says, “You people never have things in order,” I might take that home with me and turn it over in my head, but that’s because I’m the one responsible for the floor, you know? It’s not like I think the radio is sending me a message or that some random thing happened specifically for me.

I guess I notice patterns sometimes, but everybody does that. Mostly I’m just trying to figure out what people mean, and then I get sidetracked thinking about work or what I should’ve said. So… no, I haven’t really believed things were meant just for me in that way.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the patient experiences thought insertion, thought withdrawal, or thought broadcasting, which are hallmark features of schizophrenia and can help differentiate between the current candidates.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt like your thoughts were not entirely your own, like someone or something was placing thoughts into your mind or removing them, or that your thoughts were somehow being shared with others without you saying them out loud?

target_item.reason: The question asks about thought insertion, thought withdrawal, or thought broadcasting. None of the provided symptom profile items specifically cover these experiences.

patient.answer:
I don’t… I don’t think so. I mean, my thoughts feel like mine, as much as I can tell. They get crowded sometimes, and I’ll lose track of where I was going, like if I’m making the order list and then I start thinking about the endcap display and then someone’s lunch break and then—sorry, that’s not what you asked.

No, I haven’t felt like somebody is putting thoughts in or taking them out. And I don’t think people can hear them unless I say them, though sometimes I worry I’ve said something out loud when maybe I only meant to think it. But that’s more me getting mixed up, I think. Not like my thoughts are being broadcast or anything.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the patient experiences thought insertion, withdrawal, or broadcasting, which would support a diagnosis of schizophrenia (F20.8).
doctor.question: Have you ever had the experience of clearly knowing that a thought you just had wasn’t actually yours, like it was placed in your mind from somewhere else?

target_item.reason: The question is directly asking about thought insertion (believing a thought was placed in the mind from outside), which is not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
No… I don’t think I’ve had that. I mean, I’ve had thoughts pop in suddenly, like “Did I lock the office?” or “I forgot to tell someone about the sale tags,” and then I’m halfway down another trail thinking about the stockroom keys or who was closing that night.

But they still feel like my thoughts, you know? Annoying sometimes, or out of nowhere, but not like they were put there by somebody else. I can’t say I’ve clearly known a thought wasn’t mine.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced delusions of reference, which would support a diagnosis of schizophrenia (F20.8) over other candidates like schizotypal disorder (F22) or other specified schizophrenia spectrum disorder (F23.8).
doctor.question: Have you ever felt like certain things people say or do, even if they don’t seem to mean anything to others, were actually about you or meant something special for you?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about ideas of reference, where neutral comments or actions feel specially directed at the patient. The provided symptom profile does not include this symptom.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so, not in that way. I mean, sometimes I think people at work are talking around something instead of just saying it straight, like they’ll make some little comment about how the aisle looks or how “some people” don’t follow up, and I wonder if they mean me.

But that’s more work stuff, you know? Because I’m supposed to be on top of it. It’s not like I hear someone say something random and think it has some big special meaning for me. I might overthink it, sure. I do that. But I wouldn’t say I’ve really felt like ordinary things were secretly about me.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences disorganized thinking or thought insertion, which would help differentiate between the diagnostic candidates.
doctor.question: Can you tell me if you ever feel like your thoughts are completely disorganized, to the point where you can’t even follow them yourself, not just others?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Thinking_Speech
target_item.manifestation: I came in because when I try to explain inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, my words start jumping from trucks to Thursdays to the church grill to my boss’s tone, and people look at me like they can’t follow what I’m saying.
target_item.reason: The question is directly about whether my thoughts become disorganized and hard to follow, which matches disorganized thinking/speech.

patient.answer:
Yeah… that’s kind of why I came in, actually. It’s not just that other people can’t follow me. Sometimes I’m trying to explain something simple, like the inventory numbers or who’s working the weekend schedule, and my words start jumping around.

I’ll be talking about the truck delivery, then somehow I’m on Thursday, then the church grill thing, then my boss’s tone when he said something, and I can see people looking at me like… like they’ve lost the thread. And then I realize I’ve lost it too. I know what I meant to get across at the start, but it sort of scatters before I can get it out.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences thought insertion, withdrawal, or broadcasting, which would support a diagnosis of schizophrenia (F20.8).
doctor.question: Have you ever felt like your thoughts were being inserted into your mind by someone else, removed from your mind, or broadcast to others without you saying them out loud?

target_item.reason: The question is about passivity experiences such as thought insertion, thought withdrawal, and thought broadcasting, which are not covered by the listed symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
No… I don’t think that’s happened. I mean, I lose my train of thought, definitely, and sometimes it feels like a thought just disappears when I’m trying to talk, like when you go into the back room for a price gun and then forget why you walked back there.

But I wouldn’t say somebody removed it, or put it in there. And I don’t think people can hear my thoughts unless I say them. I may worry I said something wrong after the fact, like in a staff meeting, but that’s different. So… no, not like that.
